# Aurora Horizon — candidate 03

Original ModHorizon shader foundation for Minecraft Java 1.21.11 / Iris 1.10.8.
Visual target: the owner's golden forest/lake and sunset village/water references.
No code from the depicted shader packs was copied. This is an experimental
candidate, not a verified equivalent to the reference images.

Candidate 02 corrects the Iris format metadata syntax that prevented candidate 01
from compiling. Format declarations are block-comment metadata; the driver checker
now compiles the source without supplying missing format definitions.

## Implemented source

- Directional sun/moon light and warm block light, separated from ambient sky.
- 2048px, 96-block, unwarped shadow mapping; nine comparisons soften edges.
- Consistent linear/HDR intermediate lighting and one final display transform.
- Depth-based contact occlusion plus vanilla vertex ambient occlusion.
- Golden/blue sky, procedural sun/moon and a soft animated 2D cloud layer.
- Water normals, view-angle Fresnel, 48-step screen-space reflections reaching
  about 144 blocks, depth rejection, binary refinement and sky fallback.
- Approximate shallow-water absorption/refraction, sunlight highlights, depth
  haze, screen-space light shafts and restrained highlight bloom.

These describe source code, not successful in-game acceptance. Driver compilation
does not establish correct Iris uniforms, buffer ordering, materials or appearance.

## Install and first test

Select AuroraHorizon-candidate-03.zip in the isolated ModHorizon Shader Test
profile. Keep the older generated and repaired packs for comparison.

1. First inspect a tree beside grass/stone at ground level, with the sun to one
   side. Sun-facing block faces should be distinctly brighter and warmer than
   shaded ones, and the tree should cast a recognisable shadow on the ground.
2. Inspect leaf cutouts, an entity, held item, torch and particles against sky.
3. View a lake from the shoreline at a grazing angle, with nearby trees/buildings
   in view. Check actual reflected shapes, shallow beds and glass separately.
4. Compare the same camera/time with the shader off. Then check sunset, noon,
   night, rain and underwater. Capture errors and FPS as observations.

## Known limits

- Overworld only is the acceptance target; Nether/End are untested.
- Screen-space reflections cannot recover offscreen or hidden scenery. 144
  blocks is ray travel, not a guarantee of reflected-object visibility.
- A single unblended translucent layer preserves the closest submitted surface;
  overlapping glass/water stacks are not fully accumulated. Refraction is an
  approximation. Transparent shadow tint is omitted; water/glass do not cast
  solid shadows. Other translucent blocks need testing.
- Clouds are a soft 2D layer and shafts are screen-space approximations, not
  volumetric rendering or ray tracing. There is no global illumination or PBR
  normal/roughness texture workflow. Vanilla block textures remain.
- Unwarped shadow coverage prioritises clarity close to the camera; finite
  distance, bias artefacts and modest fixed-filter softness need evaluation.
- Basic debug/line programs use Iris fallback. All preservation checks remain
  pending actual game tests.

## Reuse and look controls

Keep pass order, buffer mapping, material IDs, colour-space conversion and
shadow transforms intact. The six look macros at the top of shaders/lib/common.glsl
control sun intensity, shadow fill, fog, waves, bloom and exposure. The AI should
map reference observations to these bounded controls first. Architectural edits
need compilation and repeatable in-game tests before promotion.

See the repository's docs/aurora-horizon-foundation.md for the buffer contract,
primary sources, validation evidence and promotion gate. Do not describe this
candidate as tested training ground truth until the acceptance record passes.

## Candidate 03 terrain materials

The owner's candidate-02 water look is retained. Water programs, sky, haze,
composite and final stages are unchanged. Terrain now has material-dependent
roughness/highlights (rough stone, timber, soil, metal and polished stone).
Near-camera stone/wood/soil also get bounded brightness-derived normal detail.
This is an approximation inferred from existing texture colour, not actual PBR
normal/height maps, displaced geometry or guaranteed material accuracy. Detail
fades over 16-40 blocks to limit shimmer. Foliage is not given inferred relief.

Use SURFACE_RELIEF=0 to disable the inferred detail and MATERIAL_HIGHLIGHTS=0 to
remove the added highlights. Compare cobblestone, planks, polished stone and an
iron block at close range, in sun and shadow, then recheck the approved water.

{
  "goal": "Golden sunset light that visibly shapes ordinary Minecraft blocks, with soft cast shadows, atmospheric depth and calm reflective water.",
  "referenceSummary": "Owner's two references show warm low sunlight, darker shaded block faces, trees and buildings casting shadows, peach haze and clouds, and landscape shapes reflected in water. These are appearance observations; this original candidate has no claim of matching them in game yet.",
  "pipeline": [
    "Early full-screen linear sky background into colortex0; shadow pass writes alpha-tested depth with an unwarped projection.",
    "Forward geometry writes lit linear HDR to colortex0, with separate direct, ambient and block light.",
    "Deferred copies opaque colortex0 into colortex4 before translucent rendering.",
    "Water/glass write colortex1 cleared to transparent; water traces depthtex1 and reads the opaque colortex4 snapshot.",
    "Composite combines the scene and translucent layer with contact occlusion, depth haze and screen-space shafts.",
    "Final samples highlights for bloom, applies exposure and tone mapping once, then converts to display gamma."
  ],
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "Directional lighting on ordinary blocks",
      "kind": "lighting",
      "priority": 1,
      "status": "implemented",
      "technique": "World-oriented normals and active sun/moon direction, warm direct light, separate ambient skylight and warm block-light channels, biome tint and vertex AO.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/gbuffers_terrain.fsh",
        "shaders/lib/lighting.glsl",
        "shaders/lib/geometry_fragment.glsl"
      ],
      "limitations": "Source implementation only; day/night, entities and material appearance need Iris tests. No global illumination or PBR surface relief."
    },
    {
      "name": "Soft filtered cast shadows",
      "kind": "shadows",
      "priority": 1,
      "status": "implemented",
      "technique": "2048px unwarped 96-block shadow depth map with cutout alpha, normal offset, slope bias, nine depth comparisons and distance fade; shadows attenuate direct light only.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/shadow.vsh",
        "shaders/shadow.fsh",
        "shaders/lib/lighting.glsl"
      ],
      "limitations": "Finite coverage and fixed PCF softness. Bias/cutout quality needs runtime checking; translucent coloured shadows are omitted."
    },
    {
      "name": "Recognisable landscape water reflections",
      "kind": "reflections",
      "priority": 1,
      "status": "implemented",
      "technique": "Deferred opaque-scene copy into colortex4, then 48 quadratically spaced view-space ray steps up to roughly 144 blocks using depthtex1, binary refinement, edge fading and a matching procedural sky fallback.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/deferred.fsh",
        "shaders/gbuffers_water.fsh",
        "shaders/composite.fsh"
      ],
      "limitations": "Only scenery visible in the screen buffers is available. No working reflected-object visibility or reference fidelity is claimed before Iris tests."
    },
    {
      "name": "Calm water and transparent shallows",
      "kind": "water",
      "priority": 1,
      "status": "approximation",
      "technique": "Animated world-anchored normals, Fresnel reflectivity, depth-based absorption and screen-space refraction, with material IDs separating water from glass.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/gbuffers_water.fsh",
        "shaders/block.properties"
      ],
      "limitations": "One unblended nearest translucent layer does not accumulate overlapping glass/water. No foam, caustics or displaced waves. Underwater needs testing."
    },
    {
      "name": "Golden sky and soft clouds",
      "kind": "sky",
      "priority": 2,
      "status": "approximation",
      "technique": "Sun-elevation-dependent horizon/zenith colours, solar and lunar discs and a world-oriented animated soft noise cloud plane, shared with reflection fallback.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/begin.fsh",
        "shaders/lib/common.glsl"
      ],
      "limitations": "Soft 2D cloud layer, not volumetric clouds. Initial Overworld target only; lower sky and night need visual evaluation."
    },
    {
      "name": "Atmospheric depth and contact shading",
      "kind": "atmosphere",
      "priority": 2,
      "status": "approximation",
      "technique": "Depth-reconstructed distance haze matching the sky, eight-sample contact occlusion and twelve-sample depth-occluded screen-space sunlight shafts.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/composite.fsh"
      ],
      "limitations": "No true volumetric scattering or indirect illumination. Occlusion and shafts may have screen-space artefacts."
    },
    {
      "name": "Controlled highlight glow",
      "kind": "bloom",
      "priority": 3,
      "status": "implemented",
      "technique": "Two-radius highlight-only sampling in linear HDR, followed by one exposure/filmic/display transform.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/final.fsh",
        "shaders/composite.fsh"
      ],
      "limitations": "Small fixed sampling kernel, not a multi-resolution bloom pyramid; quality and performance require runtime evaluation."
    },
    {
      "name": "Terrain material highlights and inferred relief",
      "kind": "other",
      "priority": 1,
      "status": "approximation",
      "technique": "Terrain IDs select roughness/metal response. Shadow-gated GGX-style highlights and small, bounded colour-height surface gradients add near-camera detail while shadow bias uses geometric normals.",
      "files": [
        "shaders/lib/geometry_fragment.glsl",
        "shaders/lib/geometry_vertex.glsl",
        "shaders/lib/lighting.glsl",
        "shaders/block.properties"
      ],
      "limitations": "Brightness is not measured height. No true PBR texture maps or displaced geometry; category coverage is incomplete. Close-up shimmer, material appearance and performance need in-game comparison."
    }
  ]
}
